source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.zh: 末帝，諱從珂，本姓王氏，鎮州人也。
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.literal: The Later Emperor, taboo name Congke, originally surnamed Wang, was a man of Zhen Prefecture.
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.idiomatic: The Later Emperor, taboo name Congke, originally surnamed Wang, was a native of Zhen Prefecture.

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.zh: 母宣憲皇后魏氏，以光啟元年歲在乙巳正月二十三日，生帝於平山。
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.literal: His mother was Empress Xuanxian, née Wei. In the first year of Guangqi, in the year yisi, on the twenty-third day of the first month, she gave birth to the Emperor at Pingshan.
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.idiomatic: His mother was Empress Xuanxian, née Wei. In the first year of Guangqi, in the yisi year, on the twenty-third day of the first month, she gave birth to the Emperor at Pingshan.

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.zh: 景福中，明宗為武皇騎將，略地至平山，遇魏氏，擄之，帝時年十餘歲，明宗養為己子。
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.literal: During Jingfu, Mingzong served as a mounted general of the Martial Emperor; while seizing territory he reached Pingshan, encountered Lady Wei, and carried her off. The Emperor was then a little over ten years old, and Mingzong raised him as his own son.
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.idiomatic: During Jingfu, Mingzong served as a mounted general under the Martial Emperor. While seizing territory he reached Pingshan, encountered Lady Wei, and carried her off. The Emperor was then a little over ten, and Mingzong raised him as his own son.

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.zh: 帝幼謹重寡言，及壯，長七尺餘，方頤大體，材貌雄偉，以驍果稱，明宗甚愛之。
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.literal: As a youth the Emperor was careful, grave, and sparing of speech. When grown, he stood more than seven chi tall, with a broad face and large physique; his talent and appearance were imposing, and he was famed for daring and resolution. Mingzong greatly cherished him.
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.idiomatic: As a youth the Emperor was careful, grave, and sparing of speech. When grown he stood more than seven chi tall, with a broad face and large frame; his talent and bearing were imposing, and he was famed for daring and resolution. Mingzong greatly cherished him.

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.zh: 在太原，嘗與石敬瑭因擊球同入於趙襄子之廟，見其塑像，屹然起立，帝秘之，私心自負。
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.literal: At Taiyuan, he once entered the shrine of Zhao Xiangzi together with Shi Jingtang while playing ball. They saw its sculpted image rise up stiffly to its feet. The Emperor kept this secret and secretly felt self-assured.
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.idiomatic: At Taiyuan he once entered the shrine of Zhao Xiangzi with Shi Jingtang while playing ball. They saw its sculpted image rise stiffly to its feet. The Emperor kept this secret and privately took it as a sign of his own destiny.

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.zh: 及從明宗征討，以力戰知名，莊宗嘗曰：「阿三不惟與我同齒，敢戰亦相類。」
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.literal: When he followed Mingzong on campaigns, he became renowned for fighting fiercely. Zhuangzong once said: "A San is not only of the same age as I; his readiness to fight is likewise similar."
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.idiomatic: When he followed Mingzong on campaign he became renowned for fierce fighting. Zhuangzong once said, "A San is not only my age-mate; his readiness to fight is much the same."

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.zh: 莊宗與梁軍戰於胡柳陂，兩軍俱撓，帝衛莊宗奪土山，摧驍陣，其軍復振。
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.literal: When Zhuangzong fought the Liang army at Huliupi, both armies faltered. The Emperor guarded Zhuangzong and seized the earthen hill, broke the enemy's fierce ranks, and their army rallied again.
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong fought the Liang army at Huliupi and both sides faltered, the Emperor guarded Zhuangzong, seized the earthen hill, broke the enemy's elite ranks, and their army rallied again.

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.zh: 時明宗先渡河，莊宗不悅，謂明宗曰：「公當為吾死，渡河安往？」
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.literal: At that time Mingzong crossed the river first. Zhuangzong was displeased and said to Mingzong: "You ought to die for me—where are you going, crossing the river?"
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.idiomatic: At that time Mingzong crossed the river first. Zhuangzong was displeased and said to Mingzong, "You ought to die for me—where are you going, crossing the river?"

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.zh: 明宗待罪，莊宗以帝從戰有功，由是解慍。
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.literal: Mingzong awaited punishment. Because the Emperor had distinguished himself in battle, Zhuangzong thereby set aside his anger.
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-c06665.idiomatic: Mingzong awaited punishment, but because the Emperor had distinguished himself in battle Zhuangzong set aside his anger.

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.zh: 丙子，詔河南府率京城居民之財以助賞軍。
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.literal: On bingzi, an edict ordered Henan Prefecture to levy the property of capital residents to reward the army.
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.idiomatic: On bingzi an edict ordered Henan Prefecture to levy the property of capital residents to reward the army.

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.zh: 丁丑，又詔預借居民五個月房課，不問士庶，一概施行。
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.literal: On dingchou, another edict ordered advance collection of five months' housing tax from residents, without distinction between gentry and commoners, uniformly enforced.
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.idiomatic: On dingchou another edict ordered advance collection of five months' housing tax from residents, without distinction between gentry and commoners, and applied it uniformly.

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.zh: 帝素輕財好施，自岐下為諸軍推戴，告軍士曰：「候入洛，人賞百千。」
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.literal: The Emperor had always been free with wealth and generous in giving. When the armies at Qi had raised him up, he told the soldiers: "When we enter Luoyang, each man shall receive a reward of one hundred or one thousand."
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.idiomatic: The Emperor had always been free with wealth and generous in giving. When the armies at Qi had raised him up, he told the soldiers, "When we enter Luoyang, each man shall receive a reward of one hundred or one thousand."

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.zh: 至是，以府藏空匱，於是有配率之令，京城庶士自絕者相繼。
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.literal: Now, because the treasury was empty, there arose orders for apportioned levies, and commoners of the capital who took their own lives followed one after another.
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.idiomatic: Now, because the treasury was empty, apportioned levies were ordered, and commoners of the capital who took their own lives followed one after another.

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.zh: 己卯，衛州奏，此月九日鄂王薨。
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.literal: On jimao, Weizhou reported that on the ninth day of that month the Prince of E had died.
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.idiomatic: On jimao Weizhou reported that on the ninth day of that month the Prince of E had died.

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.zh: 庚辰，以宰臣劉煦判三司。
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.literal: On gengchen, Chief Councillor Liu Xu was assigned to administer the Three Departments.
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.idiomatic: On gengchen Chief Councillor Liu Xu was assigned to administer the Three Departments.

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.zh: 辛巳，邢州奏，磁州刺史宋令詢自經而卒。
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.literal: On xinsi, Xing Prefecture reported that Song Lingxun, prefect of Ci Prefecture, had hanged himself and died.
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.idiomatic: On xinsi Xing Prefecture reported that Song Lingxun, prefect of Ci Prefecture, had hanged himself and died.

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.zh: 令詢，鄂王在藩時都押牙也，故至於是。
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.literal: Lingxun had been the prince's chief military adjutant when the Prince of E was in his fief, and so it came to this.
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.idiomatic: Lingxun had been the Prince of E's chief military adjutant when the prince was in his fief, and so it came to this.

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.zh: 甲申，帝以鄂王薨，行服於內園，群臣奉慰。
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.literal: On jiashen, because the Prince of E had died, the Emperor observed mourning in the inner garden, and the officials came to offer condolences.
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.idiomatic: On jiashen, because the Prince of E had died, the Emperor observed mourning in the inner garden and the officials came to offer condolences.

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.zh: 癸未，太后、太妃出宮中衣服器用，以助賞軍。
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.literal: On guiwei, the Empress Dowager and Imperial Consort brought forth clothing and utensils from the palace to help reward the army.
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.idiomatic: On guiwei the Empress Dowager and Imperial Consort brought forth clothing and utensils from the palace to help reward the army.

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.zh: 乙酉，帝服袞冕禦明堂殿，文武百僚朝服就位，宣製改應順元年為清泰元年，大赦天下，常赦不原者咸赦除之。
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.literal: On yiyou, the Emperor donned dark robes and the imperial cap, ascended the Hall of Bright Hall, and the civil and military officials took their places in court dress. An edict was proclaimed changing the first year of Yingshun to the first year of Qingtai, granting a great amnesty throughout the realm; even offenses normally excluded from regular amnesties were entirely pardoned.
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.idiomatic: On yiyou the Emperor donned dark robes and the imperial cap, ascended the Hall of Bright Hall, and the civil and military officials took their places in court dress. An edict was proclaimed changing the first year of Yingshun to the first year of Qingtai, granting a great amnesty throughout the realm; even offenses normally excluded from regular amnesties were entirely pardoned.

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.zh: 丁亥，以宣徽北院使郝瓊為宣徽南院使，權判樞密院；
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.literal: On dinghai, Hao Qiong, commissioner of the northern bureau of the Palace Attendants' Service, was made commissioner of the southern bureau and provisionally directed the Bureau of Military Affairs;
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.idiomatic: On dinghai Hao Qiong, commissioner of the northern bureau of the Palace Attendants' Service, was made commissioner of the southern bureau and provisionally directed the Bureau of Military Affairs;

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.zh: 以前三司使王玫為宣徽北院使。
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.literal: the former Three Departments commissioner Wang Mei was made commissioner of the northern bureau.
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.idiomatic: former Three Departments commissioner Wang Mei was made commissioner of the northern bureau.

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.zh: 以隨駕牙將宋審虔為皇城使，劉延朗為莊宅使。
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.literal: the escort military adjutant Song Shenqian was made commissioner of the Imperial City, and Liu Yanlang was made commissioner of the palace estates.
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.idiomatic: escort military adjutant Song Shenqian was made commissioner of the Imperial City, and Liu Yanlang was made commissioner of the palace estates.

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.zh: 鳳翔節度判官韓昭裔為左諫議大夫，充端明殿學士；
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.literal: the Fengxiang military governor's aide Han Zhaoyi was made Left Remonstrance and Counsel Grandee and appointed academician of the Hall of Enlightenment;
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.idiomatic: Fengxiang military governor's aide Han Zhaoyi was made Left Remonstrance and Counsel Grandee and appointed academician of the Hall of Enlightenment;

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.zh: 觀察判官馬裔孫為翰林學士；
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.literal: the surveillance commissioner's aide Ma Yisun was made Hanlin academician;
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.idiomatic: surveillance commissioner's aide Ma Yisun was made Hanlin academician;

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.zh: 掌書記李專美為樞密院直學士。
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.literal: and the chief secretary Li Zhuanmei was made direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.idiomatic: and chief secretary Li Zhuanmei was made direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.zh: 戊子，侍衛親軍都指揮使康義誠伏誅。
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.literal: On wuzi, Kang Yicheng, commander of the palace guard's personal army, was executed.
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.idiomatic: On wuzi Kang Yicheng, commander of the palace guard's personal army, was executed.

source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.zh: 是日，詔曰：樞密使朱宏昭、馮贇、宣徽南院使孟漢瓊、西京留守王思同、前邠州節度使藥彥稠，共相朋煽，妄舉干戈，互興離間之謀，幾構傾亡之禍，宜行顯戮，以快群情，仍削奪官爵雲。
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.literal: That day an edict stated: Chief military commissioners Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun, Commissioner of the Southern Bureau Meng Hanqiong, Western Capital garrison commander Wang Sitong, and former Bin Prefecture military governor Yao Yanchou banded together in conspiracy, rashly raised arms, and each stirred schemes of division—nearly bringing about the calamity of national collapse. They should receive open execution to satisfy public sentiment, and their ranks and titles shall be stripped away.
source-jiuwudaishi-046-wikisource-76363e.idiomatic: That day an edict stated: Chief military commissioners Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun, Commissioner of the Southern Bureau Meng Hanqiong, Western Capital garrison commander Wang Sitong, and former Bin Prefecture military governor Yao Yanchou banded together in conspiracy, rashly raised arms, and each stirred schemes of division—nearly bringing about the calamity of national collapse. They should receive open execution to satisfy public sentiment, and their ranks and titles were to be stripped away.
